title: Graceful latency shepherd and attention pulse scheduler
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Reduce 99th/99.9th token latency under mixed workload bursts by introducing a graceful admission policy (latency shepherd) and an attention pulse scheduler that coordinates attention-window sizing, kernel hints, and decode preemption. This ticket implements a lightweight runtime layer that: 1) applies deadline-aware admission with soft thresholds that allow controlled micro-burst acceptance; 2) emits kernel-affinity hints (float16 vs int8, fused attention path preference) early in the prefill phase; 3) dynamically adjusts attention window slices (pulse sizing) during long decodes to reduce KV cache thrash; and 4) schedules decode work in small interleaved quanta to avoid single-request monopolization of attention kernels. The design favors observability and gradual rollout: metrics for per-request kernel selection, attention-window transitions, admission rejections, and tail latency breakdowns will be added to the Console dashboards. This is an engineering-first change intended to be transparent to API consumers but tunable by runtime config and per-customer policies.
acceptance_criteria: P99 token latency reduced by >=15% on mixed short+long workload synthetic trace compared to baseline runtime-1.18 under same capacity
Admission rejects/deferrals account for <1% of requests at steady state; transient deferrals measurable and documented
No regression in median latency or throughput for 95% of customer traffic (verified via canary)
Kernel-affinity hints are recorded on traces and match the kernel chosen >=90% of the time
Feature gated and rolloutable via runtime config flags; can be disabled per-tenant
updates: 2025-02-20 - Triage: Raised after customer incident showing 99.9th token spikes during mixed workloads. Initial spike analysis points to attention kernel starvation and large prefill decode bursts.

2025-02-24 - Architecture: Decided on two coordinated pieces: (A) Latency Shepherd (deadline buckets + soft-admission + cheap fast-path kernel hints), (B) Attention Pulse Scheduler (dynamic window sizing + decode time-slicing). Chosen to keep admission logic O(1) per request to avoid extra queuing overhead.

2025-02-27 - Prototype: Implemented a proof-of-concept in the local runtime sandbox: simple deadline buckets (fast/normal/elastic) and a pulse controller that reduces attention window by 25% for requests in the elastic bucket. Early microbench shows 12% drop in P99 for synthetic mix. Patch: branch pulse-admission-proto.

2025-03-01 - Experiment: Ran canary on two nodes with real traffic sample (20% traffic). Observed 18% reduction in P99 for short requests, but a 4% increase in 95th for very long decodes due to aggressive window shrinking. Tuned pulse aggressiveness and added backoff histograms.

2025-03-03 - Kernel hints: Added kernel-affinity metadata to prefill handshake so the scheduler can try to pick fused-attention kernels when attention-window > threshold. Integration tests show affinity honored in 92% of cases; remaining mismatches tracked to quantization path fallback.

2025-03-05 - Review: PR #4678 created. Requesting PM and SRE feedback for rollout plan and dashboarding. Noted that fallback to int8 path increases token cost by ~6% for affected requests; need PM alignment on cost tradeoffs for default policy. Preparing A/B canary plan for next week.
notes: Trade-offs considered: aggressive admission reduces tails but can increase visible rejections — chose soft deferrals with transparent retry guidance to clients.

Kernel selection strategy: prefer fused-attn float16 for medium-length windows; fall back to quantized kernels when memory pressure detected. This required small additions to kernel registry API for runtime hints.
Observability: added tags to traces: admission_bucket, pulse_version, kernel_affinity, attention_window_ratio. These are included in canary dashboards to analyze regressions per version.
